executive_assessment.text: Béchar's 2024 flood and Oran's coastal storm exposure provide named cases. Broader heat and drought evidence distinguishes coastal, Saharan and steppe settings without inventing wilaya-specific values.

Historical disaster-risk-finance gaps and intended Algiers studies describe coping and institutional constraints. Proposed fiscal reforms and statutory warning/planning requirements are not verified implementation outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-07-03 reports: The assessment reports September 2024 flooding displaced 280 families in Béchar and damaged roads and electricity infrastructure in southern and western Algeria.
Source dated 2023 reports: The diagnostic says coastal storms particularly affect the Oran coastline, damaging port infrastructure, maritime transport and aquaculture farms.

Source dated 2002-07-18 reports: Annex names Hamiz Oued, Oued El Harrach, Ouchaiah Oued, Kniss Oued and Telemly for a flood, landslide, seismic and pollution study; it proposes separate catchment-basin work for Bouzareah.

Source dated 2002-07-18 reports: After the 2001 Algiers flood, the Wilaya of Algiers and public agencies, administrations and residents provided emergency measures and temporary relief that partly mitigated immediate impacts.

Source dated 2002-07-18 reports: The project design proposed a meteorological monitoring and early-warning system in Algiers for possible national expansion and training for civil protection, water-resources and meteorology agencies.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 13 of 13 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No existing DZA country baseline was present in the worktree.
The IMF climate-to-displacement pathway is projected risk framing, not measured migration, intergroup tension or conflict.
No country-specific evidence was found that conflict or insecurity has disrupted climate adaptation or service delivery; this is not evidence of absence.
The National Climate Plan PDF exceeded web extraction size limits and its Ministry download page timed out; no claims rely on search snippets.
IEA heat ranges cover unnamed groups of coastal and southern wilayas; the report does not provide named-wilaya values in the cited passage.
The 2002 World Bank annex documents intended studies and training but not implementation results.
Projected mobility pressure on the northern coast is not treated as conflict or violence. No full mediated FCV pathway is assembled from the retrieved evidence.
Statutory requirements are reported as written in the 2024 law, not as a legal compliance assessment or proof that local plans function.
